  PROBLEM: Scanning each piped producer word independently fails to associate credential flags with values split across quoted words, which can leak credentials or unnecessarily withhold the command.
  WHY: The scanner can miss values such as `mycustompwd` when the flag and value are separate words; minimax_minimax-m3 reports a related case that is withheld instead of leaked.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py (and workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py): 796 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `_shell_runner_before` treats any shell-runner name anywhere in a pipeline segment as the command, so a positional argument such as `sh` can trigger parsing of producer text as a shell script.
  WHY: Benign commands can raise `ValueError` during that parsing and be withheld; deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro and google_gemini-3_8-flash rated this MAJOR, while openai_gpt-6-luna and z-ai_glm-5_2 rated it NIT.

  WHY: `_sanitize_bash_command` can return the display text unchanged and `record_example` can post the password in the issue body and consumer PR or issue.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py (and workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py): 796 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `_shell_runner_before(segment, 0, len(segment))` scans every word, including positional arguments, and can treat an argument such as `sh` as a shell runner.
  WHY: A benign command with an unmatched quote can raise `ValueError` during parsing and be withheld; the same over-broad check at line 783 affects the here-string path.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py (and workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py): 797-798 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Piped producer words are passed individually to `_command_line_credentials`, so a credential flag and its value in separate words are not linked.
  WHY: The credential can remain visible in the returned display text and posted report because `redact` does not catch the quoted form.

  PROBLEM: In a multi-stage pipeline, `piped_words` is overwritten at each pipe, losing words from earlier stages before the final shell runner is reached.
  WHY: Earlier producer credentials may not be masked; the source says the practical effect is over-withholding or a shape that does not reflect the inner command's true structure, while noting the fail-closed default.

  PROBLEM: Each piped word is scanned separately, so a credential flag and value spanning multiple quoted arguments are not linked.
  WHY: The example produces only the short value `"u"`, below `MIN_MASKED_VALUE_CHARS=4`, and the command is withheld; the source says the actual password is not posted.
- .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py (and workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py): `_command_line_credentials()`, the pipe handling guard `if piped_words and _shell_runner_before(segment, 0, len(segment))`
  PROBLEM: `_shell_runner_before` checks every word in the segment, so a shell name used as a positional argument can trigger the piped-word scan.
  WHY: The visible input ends while describing the example `echo "curl -u" "deploy:pw" | grep sh`; it identifies `"sh"` as a grep search pattern, not the command. (Input truncated.)
